newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS' BOONSTRA OUTLINES RECOVERY TARGETS.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS' BOONSTRA OUTLINES RECOVERY TARGETS.

text.p: Philips Electronics said on Thursday that a one billion guilder fourth quarter restructuring was set to achieve double-digit growth in 1997 income from operations (IFO).
"We're looking for sustainable double digit IFO growth...and targeting 24 percent RONA (Return on Net Operating (capital) (Assets)," new president Cor Boonstra told a news conference.
In addition, Philips would seek to generate a positive cashflow of one billion guilders during 1997, Boonstra said.
Philips earlier posted a 69 percent slump in third quarter income from operations (before financial income and tax) to 281 million guilders from 922 million in the year-earlier period.
The company is at present generating a return on net operating capital of 8.4 percent, down from 18 percent in the comparable 1995 quarter.
Third quarter net earnings from normal operations fell by 77 percent to 123 million guilders, just over half the lowest analyst's estimate.
Philips declined to give a full-1996 profit forecast, but said it would take a one-billion guilder charge in the fourth quarter to accelerate restructuring.
Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast third quarter earnings of 240-360 million guilders.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
